interactions_checked.interaction: Additive risk of hyperkalaemia and worsening renal function
interactions_checked.action: Check serum K+ and creatinine before start; monitor K+ 1‑2 weeks after initiation and after any dose change; hold if K+ >5.0 mmol/L or creatinine rises >30%.

interactions_checked.interaction: Thiazide may cause hypokalaemia which can offset MRA‑induced hyperkalaemia, but combined monitoring required
interactions_checked.action: Monitor electrolytes closely; adjust thiazide dose if needed.

interactions_checked.interaction: Both lower blood pressure and increase diuresis → risk of hypotension and volume depletion
interactions_checked.action: Measure BP and volume status before initiation; start at full dose but counsel on adequate hydration; monitor BP after 1‑2 weeks.

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined diuretic effect may cause dehydration, electrolyte disturbances, and hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Monitor BP, electrolytes and renal function after start; consider reducing thiazide dose if signs of volume depletion.

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive natriuresis → higher risk of volume depletion and acute kidney injury
interactions_checked.action: Close monitoring of weight, BP, renal function; adjust loop diuretic dose as needed.

interactions_checked.interaction: Tacrolimus inhibits CYP3A4, increasing simvastatin plasma concentrations → risk of myopathy/rhabdomyolysis
interactions_checked.action: Consider switching to pravastatin 10‑20 mg daily or reducing simvastatin to 5 mg; check CK if muscle symptoms develop.

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential increase in metoprolol levels leading to bradycardia/hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Observe heart rate and blood pressure after any dose change; adjust metoprolol if clinically indicated.

assumptions_warnings: eGFR values are 28.2 and 20.2 mL/min/1.73 m²; current estimate assumed ~20 mL/min – all renal‑dose adjustments made accordingly.
Serum potassium, sodium, and bicarbonate not provided – baseline labs required before starting spironolactone and after any dose change.
Blood pressure not recorded – must measure before titrating ACE‑I, beta‑blocker, SGLT2‑i, or adding diuretics.
Left ventricular ejection fraction not documented – echocardiogram required to confirm HFrEF (LVEF ≤40%) before applying HFrEF‑specific drugs.
Glucose is low (65 mg/dL) – monitor for hypoglycaemia after initiating SGLT2‑i, especially if any glucose‑lowering agents are added later.
Statin‑tacrolimus interaction noted; consider switching to pravastatin or dose reduction.
Patient is a current smoker using nicotine patch; smoking may increase heart rate and counteract beta‑blocker effect – encourage cessation and monitor HR.
treatment_summary: The patient is a 90‑year‑old man with CKD stage 4, hypertension, ischaemic heart disease and likely HFrEF. Existing ACE‑I (lisinopril) and beta‑blocker (metoprolol) satisfy two of the four NICE first‑line disease‑modifying drugs. Add spironolactone 12.5 mg daily and dapagliflozin 10 mg daily (both first‑line per NICE NG106) after confirming normal potassium and stable renal function. Introduce a low‑dose loop diuretic (furosemide 20 mg) only if clinical congestion is present. Monitor renal function, electrolytes, blood pressure and weight closely, obtain an echocardiogram to verify HFrEF, and adjust the statin regimen due to tacrolimus interaction. Avoid NSAIDs, verapamil, diltiazem, thiazolidinediones and class I antiarrhythmics. Provide standard non‑pharmacological advice (fluid/salt restriction, exercise, vaccinations, smoking cessation).
